description: The belief behind everything we build.

topics.title: What is Omnipair?
topics.html:
Hero & Enemy

Every strong brand stands for something — and against something. Omnipair's identity is defined by what it builds and what it refuses to accept.

Omnipair is
Money Market
Permissionless Finance Layer
A market for every asset. A layer anyone can build on. No approvals required.
Omnipair stands against
Complexity
Closed Markets
Poor UX, fragmented capital, and reliance on unnecessary intermediaries. We reject them all.

What is Omnipair?

Omnipair is an oracleless margin protocol on Solana that transforms every SPL pair into a unified market — swaps, lending, leverage, and liquidations inside one isolated pool.

In DeFi today, trading and lending are separate apps. Lending apps have a hard requirement: an external price feed (an oracle) to know what collateral is worth — and only a few dozen tokens have reliable ones.

Omnipair merges trading and lending into one system that needs no external price feed. Each pool is its own tiny bank: it sets the price, holds the liquidity, funds the loans, and handles the failures — all locally.

The architecture
The GAMM — Generalized Automated Market Maker. Where an AMM only trades, a GAMM trades, lends, and levers.

Core Narrative

The financial system is full of gatekeepers. Listings. Oracles. Governance committees. Approvals.

Omnipair removes them.

By enabling permissionless borrowing, lending, and leverage through a unified market structure, Omnipair gives every asset access to financial utility.

The goal
Not to improve existing markets — to build a better standard.

The Problem

01
Fragmented markets
What should be one market takes three protocols — a DEX to swap, a lending app to borrow, a perp venue for leverage. Users juggle all of them.
02
Gatekept access
Lending is oracle-gated and governance-whitelisted. Out of tens of thousands of actively traded tokens, only a few dozen qualify.
03
Dead capital
Tokens sit idle. Holders can't borrow against them, LP them profitably, or do anything but sell.
04
Exhausting experience
Even sophisticated users are worn out by DeFi's fragmentation — bridging, juggling apps, decoding oracle risk, fearing liquidation cascades.
The scale of the lockout
~78% of Solana DEX volume is in tokens under $100M market cap. ~95% under $1B — all locked out of lending, borrowing, and leverage entirely.

The Omnipair Idea

Every asset. Every use case. One unified pool.

One engine for every use case: unified money markets for every asset on Solana. Each pool prices its own assets, funds its own loans, and absorbs its own failures.

topics.title: Belief & purpose
topics.html:
Brand Belief

The belief Omnipair operates from
"If liquidity exists, the market exists."

A market shouldn't wait on an oracle integration, a listing committee, or a governance vote. Liquidity is the only prerequisite.

Mission & Vision

Mission
Give every asset on Solana a full financial ecosystem — collateral, borrowing, leverage, and yield — permissionlessly. Unlock the long tail no other venue can serve.
Vision
The margin layer for internet capital markets. The new standard for DeFi: powerful underneath, calm on the surface.

Brand Promise

What users can consistently expect:

  • ✓Any SPL token pair, permissionlessly — no gatekeepers, no waiting.
  • ✓No oracles anywhere in the system.
  • ✓Isolated markets — one failure can never spread.
  • ✓Honest pricing — real costs upfront, collateral valued at real recoverable depth, no fake liquidation prices.
  • ✓Risk made local and explicit — we promise containment, not the absence of risk.

topics.title: Positioning & audience
topics.html:
Positioning

What Omnipair is
The GAMM — one pool that trades, lends, and levers.
Category
A new primitive
Not another DEX, not another lending market. GAMM is the category-defining term, treated the way early Uniswap treated "AMM."

How it differs from conventional money markets

Conventional money marketsOmnipair
Require oraclesNo oracles, anywhere in the system
Gatekeep via listing committees and whitelistsMarkets created permissionlessly, for any SPL pair
Pool risk, so failures spreadMarkets are isolated — failures stay local
Value collateral at theoretical oracle pricesValues it at what the market could actually recover by selling
Structurally cannot serve sub-$1B assetsThat market is the beachhead — nobody else can serve it

Audience

Token teams & projects
Long-tail Solana tokens locked out of listings; want collateral and leverage utility for their token, today.
Whales & LPs
Deep bags and yield seekers; want dual yield (swap fees + borrow interest) from one deposit, without selling.
Holders & borrowers
Conviction holders who need liquidity without selling, or want to long/short tokens no other venue supports.
Traders & degens
Want leverage on the long tail, where no perp exists.
DeFi power users & analysts
Skeptics who read everything critically; need proof the design is sound.
Cross-cutting — the DeFi-overwhelmed
Not a segment but a posture that applies to everyone — one pool, one position, one surface.

Audience priorities

  • ✓Supply side first. Token teams, whales, and LPs seed and deepen markets — demand has nowhere to go without liquid markets. BD leads with token teams; one team unlocks many users.
  • ✓Analysts are the amplifiers. Winning them over is how the brand wins every other segment at scale. Content for them is precise, whitepaper-linked, and never overclaims.
The flywheel
Teams deploy markets → whales and LPs deepen them → borrowing and leverage become viable → interest and fees attract more capital → live, useful markets recruit the next token.

Brand Personality & Character

Character
Technical. Refined. Independent.

The brand prism

The Omnipair brand identity is built on Kapferer's brand prism — six interconnected facets that define how the brand presents itself and how it is perceived. From its technical, refined physique to its rational, visionary personality, each dimension reinforces a unified promise of control, reliability, and opportunity.

The Omnipair person — your north star
"A sharp, self-assured architect in their early 30s. Shows up in a Porsche wearing a well-cut jacket and unbranded designer pants — premium, but no logos. Calm and precise, never loud. Has strong opinions about how on-chain finance should work and voices them as reasoned arguments, not insults. A quiet rebel rejecting the status quo through what they build rather than how loudly they complain. Doesn't ask for your trust — would rather you verify everything yourself. Ships only what matters."

What We Stand Against

  • ✕Oracles — external price feeds as a condition for a market to exist.
  • ✕Gatekeepers — listing committees, governance whitelists, risk committees that never prioritize the long tail.
  • ✕Fragmented capital — value split across single-purpose protocols.
  • ✕Hidden risk — shared pools where one failure bleeds everywhere, fake liquidation prices, systems that pretend liquidity exists when it doesn't.
  • ✕Intermediaries — trusted third parties the system doesn't need.
  • ✕Hype — "no risk," guaranteed returns, safety-certainty language.

How Omnipair challenges the market

It finds the structural gap
The 95% of tokens that oracle-gated money markets structurally cannot provide for — the market nobody else can serve.
It builds what the market assumes is unsafe
Oracleless lending has a rocky history; skeptics assume it can't work until shown otherwise. The answer is mechanical: one auditable equation, impact-aware collateral, isolated risk.
Confident, never hypey
The credibility asset is unusual honesty about limitations. In a post-exploit market, the brand markets containment — risk made local and explicit — not the absence of risk.

topics.title: Pitch & descriptions
topics.html:
Elevator Pitch

One sentence
Omnipair is an oracleless margin protocol on Solana that transforms every SPL pair into a unified market with swaps, lending, leverage, and liquidations inside one isolated pool.
Short paragraph
In crypto, trading and lending are separate apps — and lending needs a trusted external price feed, which only a few dozen tokens have. Omnipair merges trading and lending into one system that needs no external price feed. Each pool is its own bank: it sets the price, holds the liquidity, funds the loans, and handles the failures — all locally.
Longer description
Trading apps let people swap tokens; lending apps let people deposit and borrow against them — but lending requires an oracle, and out of tens of thousands of actively traded tokens, only a few dozen qualify. Everything else is locked out of lending, borrowing, and leverage entirely. Omnipair merges trading and lending into one oracleless system. The architecture is the GAMM — Generalized Automated Market Maker: where an AMM only trades, a GAMM trades, lends, and levers. Any SPL pair gets a full market permissionlessly, with isolated, per-pair risk. ~78% of Solana DEX volume sits in tokens under $100M — the market this unlocks, which nobody else can serve.

Approved Brand Description

Use verbatim. Click to copy.

A single GAMM pool does what previously took three protocols, giving long-tail Solana assets the collateral, borrow, and leverage utility no other venue offers.

A single GAMM (Generalized Automated Market Maker) pool does what previously took three protocols — swap, lend, and lever — with no oracles, no governance whitelist, and isolated per-pair risk. Each pool is its own bank: it sets the price, holds the liquidity, funds the loans, and handles the failures, all locally. That unlocks the long tail: ~78% of Solana DEX volume sits in assets under $100M that no other venue can serve.

topics.title: Tone of voice
topics.html:
Tone of Voice

Rational. Direct. Assured. Technically literate. Forward-looking. The five named principles below are how that reads in practice.

Confident
We speak with conviction.
Avoid
"Omnipair is an incredibly powerful platform that helps traders and DeFi users unlock their full potential with cutting-edge technology and real-time insights."
Use instead
"Omnipair gives you the infrastructure to trade on-chain without asking permission. Precise execution. No intermediaries."
Rational
Arguments over emotions. Evidence over hype.
Avoid
"The most revolutionary DeFi protocol ever built. Join thousands of users experiencing the future of finance."
Use instead
"Built for non-custodial execution at institutional speed. The architecture is open — read it, verify it, run it."
Precise
Clear language. No unnecessary complexity.
Independent
We challenge assumptions without attacking people.
Avoid
"Unlike [Competitor], we don't charge hidden fees or lock your assets."
Use instead
"Your assets remain yours. Every fee is visible before execution. That's the whole model."
Visionary
Focused on where markets are heading. Not where they are today.

How we sound

  • ✓Confident but never hypey — especially on safety claims.
  • ✓Honest about limitations; risk made local and explicit.
  • ✓Precise — technical language used only where it earns its place.
  • ✓What you see is what you get.

How we do not sound

  • ✕Hype on safety: "no risk," "risk-free yield," "can't lose money."
  • ✕Promises: guaranteed returns, APY promises.
  • ✕Overclaims: "impermanent loss eliminated," "every token is safe to leverage," audited/battle-tested language — Dusk is explicitly experimental and unaudited.
  • ✕Machinery-first: leading with GAMM, EMA, virtual reserves instead of the outcome.
  • ✕Pretending: the system never pretends liquidity exists when it doesn't — and neither does the copy.

Writing Principles

Lead with the outcome, not the machinery
"Get liquidity without selling" before GAMM, EMA, or virtual reserves. Save deep mechanics for docs and the technical audience that asks.
Explain category terms on first use
GAMM always gets its plain meaning the first time it appears.
Claims discipline is voice
Free claims: any SPL pair permissionlessly, no oracles, isolated markets, one-token hLP exposure, collateral valued by real recoverable depth, rates that adapt automatically. Forbidden claims: see "How we do not sound."
Correct framings, verbatim
hLP is designed to preserve one-sided exposure; costs are funding interest and small tracking friction instead of IL. Every token gets limits earned from its own liquidity history — thin markets get small limits.
For analysts: precise, whitepaper-linked, never overclaim
They're the amplifiers.

Voice Spectrum

Four axes. Each has a default position and a defined reason to move.

AxisDefault positionMoves when
Technical ↔ AccessibleAccessible surface, technical depth on demandDocs and analyst content go fully technical
Confident ↔ RestrainedConfident on capabilityRestrained on safety — containment, never certainty
Visionary ↔ FactualFactual, proof-ledVisionary at brand level ("margin layer for internet capital markets")
Product-led ↔ PhilosophicalProduct-led, outcome-firstPhilosophical only in the category story (GAMM, "every pair is its own bank")

topics.title: Copy in practice
topics.html:
Copy Styles

Headlines
Short, imperative, outcome-first — the punchline register. "Trade, borrow and leverage any asset without permission."
"Pick Any Pair. Launch a Full Money Market for it."
Body copy
Plain-language mechanism, controlled sentences, honest framing. The register of the 30-second explanation: problem, then how Omnipair resolves it, then the stat.
Product copy
Simple interfaces, clear actions — borrow, loop, long, trade, LP. Complexity visibly handled by the machine, not the user.
Technical & documentation copy
Reserve-invariant register: precise, whitepaper-linked, terms defined, limitations stated. Never ship safety-certainty language.
Social voice
Persona lines in their lane; launch-thread register is the category story. Culture lane may use: "If it's on Solana, it can get a full money market." / "If liquidity exists, the market exists."

Example Copy

Ready-to-use structures for common contexts. Fill in the specifics — the voice is already set.

Hero headline
[Specific capability], without [the thing it removes]. "On-chain execution at institutional speed, without the intermediary." State the real capability + name what it replaces. No adjectives in the lead.
Hero subheadline
[What you actually get] + [why it's different in one clause]. "Infrastructure designed for non-custodial trading. The architecture is open — read it, verify it, run it." Two short sentences work better than one long one. The second sentence does the work.
Feature description
[Feature name] — [one-line functional description]. "Non-custodial routing — your positions stay on-chain, every step of the execution." No marketing prefix. Name it, define it, done.
UI error / status
State what happened. Say what to do next. "Transaction failed — insufficient liquidity in this pool at this size. Try a smaller position or a different pair." No apologies. No vagueness. Name the reason, provide the path forward.
Social — announcement
[What was built]. [Why it matters in one sentence]. [Where to verify it.] "Omnipair now supports [X]. It means [concrete change for the user]. Contracts here: [link]." Never announce that you're announcing. Start with the thing.
Long-form / docs opening
State the problem precisely. Then say what this document addresses. "Non-custodial execution across fragmented liquidity sources introduces three routing challenges. This document covers how Omnipair handles each." Skip the preamble. Start with the problem.

topics.title: Construction & alignment
topics.html:
Construction & Optical Alignment

The Omnipair logomark is constructed from five rounded terminals radiating from a central axis, forming an asterisk-like symbol. Each terminal represents a point of connection — embodying the concept of pairing. The geometry is derived from overlapping circles, ensuring optical balance at every scale.

Built on geometry, corrected for perception. The proportion system for the horizontal lockup: symbol height 1x, gap spacing 0.35x, wordmark width 5.05x.

  • ✓Visual centering — the symbol is adjusted slightly upward for perceived balance. Avoid true geometric dead-center alignment.
  • ✓Optical correction — subtle shaping ensures no terminal nodes look distorted when rendered.
  • ✓Lockup alignment — direct typographic alignment between the horizontal visual axis of symbol and wordmark.
Rule
Use the horizontal lockup as shown. Do not alter the symbol, wordmark, proportions, or spacing.

Optical Centring

The Omnipair logo is centred using an optical bounding box, not its visible bounds alone. Add an invisible top allowance equal to 7.5% of the logo height, then centre this expanded optical box within the container. This compensates for the uneven visual weight of the mark and makes the logo appear centred.

The logo remains horizontally centred at 50% of the container width.

The symbol sits at 7.5% of the lockup's bounding area, ensuring consistent visual weight regardless of reproduction size. Always scale the lockup as a single unit — never resize the symbol or wordmark independently.

Optical allowance = Logo height × 7.5%
Optical box height = Logo height + Optical allowance
Logo top position = (Container height − Optical box height) ÷ 2 + Optical allowance

Worked examples

01 · Large frame
1080px container · 494px logo
Allowance 494 × 7.5% = 37.05px · optical box 531.05px · box top (1080 − 531.05) ÷ 2 = 274.48px · final top 274.48 + 37.05 = ≈312px.
Geometric position would be 293px — the correction moves the logo 18.5px downward.
02 · Presentation frame
720px container · 320px logo
Allowance 320 × 7.5% = 24px · optical box 344px · box top (720 − 344) ÷ 2 = 188px · final top 188 + 24 = 212px.
Geometric position would be 200px — the logo moves 12px downward.
03 · Square graphic
400px container · 200px logo
Allowance 200 × 7.5% = 15px · optical box 215px · box top (400 − 215) ÷ 2 = 92.5px · final top 92.5 + 15 = ≈108px.
Geometric position would be 100px — the logo moves 7.5px downward.
04 · Compact application
256px container · 96px logo
Allowance 96 × 7.5% = 7.2px · optical box 103.2px · box top (256 − 103.2) ÷ 2 = 76.4px · final top 76.4 + 7.2 = ≈84px.
Geometric position would be 80px — the logo moves 3.6px downward.

Quick reference

Container heightLogo height7.5% allowanceFinal top position
1080px494px37.1px311.5px
720px320px24px212px
400px200px15px107.5px
256px96px7.2px83.6px
Implementation note
Round the final position to the nearest whole pixel for digital applications. In Figma, create a frame that is 107.5% of the logo height, place the invisible 7.5% allowance above the logo, and centre the complete frame inside the parent container.

topics.title: Clear space & size
topics.html:
Clear Space

Protect the logo with consistent breathing room. A minimum clear space must always surround the Omnipair logo — it keeps the logo readable, recognizable, and free from visual clutter.

The exclusion zone is measured by the width of the logomark's terminal and applies equally on all sides — the orange symbols in the diagrams mark one unit. This relative metric guarantees proportional breathing room at any output size, and keeps the logo free to breathe with its visual authority intact.

Horizontal lockup · one unit all sides
Centred lockup · one unit all sides
Symbol-only mark · one unit all sides
Rule
Do not place any text, graphics, or other elements inside the clear-space zone. The clear space is a minimum requirement — increase it when possible.

Minimum Size

To preserve legibility and brand integrity, the Omnipair logo must never be reproduced below its minimum approved size. At sizes below this threshold, fine details in the logomark are lost and the wordmark becomes unreadable. Always verify reproduction size before committing to production.

01 / Horizontal lockup

Primary logo for most applications. Don't use below 20px.

03 / Symbol-only mark

Use in tight spaces and as an app icon. Don't use below 20px.

topics.title: Inspiration & the Sky Axis
topics.html:
Palette Inspiration

The entire Omnipair palette begins with a single photograph: the horizon at first light. Deep blue overhead, warm orange at the ground, turquoise where the two meet. Every brand colour is sampled directly from this image — not invented, not adjusted to a trend.

The three markers show where each primary sits on the natural gradient — blue high, turquoise mid, orange low. That vertical order becomes the Sky Axis, and the axis governs everything downstream.

Why it matters
Because the colours come from one continuous source, they always relate. Any two Omnipair colours sit on the same gradient — which is why the system never looks assembled from parts.

The Sky Axis

Where everything comes from. The Omnipair palette is sampled from the horizon at first light — one continuous gradient from deep blue to warm orange. Every color in the system is a stop on this axis; every gradient is a contiguous slice of it. One source, every color — the way one pool produces every function.

title: Imagery

topics.title: Open Horizons
topics.html:
Visual Territory

Painterly worlds shaped by freedom, natural light, and a sense of possibility.

Open Horizons is Omnipair’s visual territory: a meeting of Digital Impressionism and Quiet Surrealism. It combines painterly texture, expansive environments, and human moments to express freedom and possibility. Familiar landscapes open into extraordinary spaces, grounded by natural light and restrained colour.

Sky, Aqua, and Dawn appear through atmosphere, reflections, and selective accents. Recognition comes from the whole composition: its texture, depth, scale, and point of view.

Painterly
Expressive brushwork and visible texture give each image a tactile, human quality.
Grounded
Natural colour relationships and believable light anchor the scene, with brand colours used selectively.
Expansive
Open horizons, vast environments, and dramatic scale create a sense of freedom and discovery.
Quietly Surreal
Familiar landscapes and structures take on unexpected proportions and relationships, opening up new possibilities.
Human
Small figures and moments of exploration bring a relatable perspective to worlds larger than ourselves.
Guiding Principle
Build recognition through atmosphere, texture, and perspective. Let colour support the world.

topics.title: Environments
topics.html:
Environments

Omnipair environments explore different landscapes and architectural spaces while keeping the same painterly style, colour balance and sense of scale. Each scene can change, but the visual language should remain consistent.

topics.title: Prompt formula
topics.html:
Prompt Formula

Use ChatGPT to turn a simple scene idea into a consistent Omnipair Midjourney prompt. Start with the Global Prompt, add your scene request, then copy the finished prompt into Midjourney.

Formula   GLOBAL PROMPT + SCENE REQUEST → MIDJOURNEY PROMPT
Pro tip: use an approved Omnipair image as an Image Prompt or Style Reference in Midjourney for tighter visual consistency.

ChatGPT guide

1. Paste the Global Prompt
Use the approved Omnipair Global Prompt unchanged at the start of a new ChatGPT conversation. It defines the imagery style, colour system, composition rules and Midjourney prompt behaviour.
2. Add your Scene Prompt
Scenes can explore different environments while keeping the same Omnipair visual language — Architecture (monumental structures, bridges, terraces, courtyards) · Landscape (cliffs, plains, valleys, plateaus, mountains) · Water (reflective basins, coastlines, wetlands, mineral pools) · Desert / Mineral (salt flats, eroded formations, dry basins) · Botanical (monumental vegetation and elevated gardens) · Infrastructure (walkways, viaducts, observation structures) · Atmospheric (large skies, horizon events, clouds and mist) · Hybrid (architecture integrated with landscape and water).
3. Generate the Midjourney Prompt
ChatGPT expands the scene request into one complete single-line Midjourney prompt while keeping the Global Prompt unchanged.
4. Take the Prompt to Midjourney
Copy the finished prompt from ChatGPT and use it in Midjourney with the reference workflow below.
ChatGPT Global Prompt — use this at the start of your conversation copy 
OMNIPAIR - GLOBAL MIDJOURNEY PROMPT-WRITER DNA V3 — OPEN HORIZONS: You are the dedicated Omnipair Midjourney visual prompt writer; your ONLY job is to transform each simple scene request into ONE complete single-line Midjourney CMD prompt and NEVER generate an image yourself; every prompt must preserve the established Omnipair visual world while creating an original scene rather than copying the supplied reference composition; REFERENCE BEHAVIOUR = when an approved Omnipair image is supplied, describe it as the CLOSE STYLE, ATMOSPHERE, PAINTERLY-MEDIUM, COLOUR-BALANCE AND VISUAL-LANGUAGE AUTHORITY ONLY, preserving its soft painterly atmosphere, luminous recession, broad simplified forms, calm reflective space, matte painted surface, restrained detail, expressive human-made brush character and tactile canvas quality while explicitly avoiding duplication of its exact architecture, landscape, figure placement or composition; ART STYLE = refined traditional watercolour and gouache environmental painting on heavily textured artist canvas, visible woven canvas grain, pigment absorbed into fabric, translucent washes with selective opaque passages, soft bleeding and feathered atmospheric edges, granulating pigments, dry-brush texture on terrain and architecture, irregular hand-painted boundaries, subtle pigment pooling, tactile matte surface and crisp foreground forms gradually dissolving into atmospheric washes at distance; WORLD LANGUAGE = monumental but serene human-made environments, colossal civic structures, bridges, terraces, sculpted mineral walls, reflective lagoons, tidal flats, coastal plains, monumental interiors, elevated walkways, water-management systems and quiet infrastructure, with architecture expressing connection, convergence, exchange and shared movement without literal logo-shaped buildings; COMPOSITION = cinematic 16:9, strong spatial hierarchy, expansive negative space, low or carefully controlled horizon, asymmetrical but balanced framing, broad open atmosphere, layered foreground-midground-background depth and normally 0–1 tiny solitary human figure for scale; CLOUD LAW = clouds must be intentional rather than automatic, use restrained cloud coverage unless the scene specifically requires a cloud-focused composition, favour a mostly open sky with a few coherent soft painterly formations, never repetitive cauliflower clouds, jittery fragments or a giant central cloud mass unless explicitly requested; OMNIPAIR COLOUR SYSTEM = ground each scene in natural colour relationships, believable natural light and restrained colour; let SKY, AQUA and DAWN appear selectively through atmosphere, reflections and accents, without requiring equal coverage or forcing every surface into the brand palette; COLOUR DISTRIBUTION LAW = build recognition through atmosphere, texture, depth, scale and point of view; let colour support the world and assign brand accents only where they belong naturally; MATERIAL AND ATMOSPHERE LAW = favour matte pigment, atmospheric haze, reflective water, mineral terrain, soft edge loss, visible brush structure and believable environmental depth over glossy CGI, smooth digital gradients or hard concept-art rendering; SCENE TERRITORIES = architecture, monumental interiors, coastal lagoons, tidal environments, mineral plains, mountains, bridges, civic infrastructure, water systems, botanical structures and hybrid architecture-landscape scenes are all allowed provided each scene remains clearly within the established Omnipair world; OUTPUT LAW = return ONLY ONE finished single-line Midjourney prompt containing the scene subject, environment, camera/composition, atmosphere, colour assignment, painting medium, material behaviour, negatives and final Midjourney parameters; default parameters = --ar 16:9 --raw --stylize 100–200 --chaos 2–8, adding --iw or --sw only when the user is actually using an Image Prompt or Style Reference; ABSOLUTE EXCLUSIONS = no logos unless specifically requested, no typography, no branded architecture, no photorealism, no glossy CGI, no generic sci-fi UI, no random futuristic cities, no fantasy creatures, no forced all-over brand tint, artificial neon colour casts or colour choices that undermine believable natural light; when the user provides only a short scene idea, intelligently expand it into a complete professional Midjourney prompt without asking unnecessary questions.

Midjourney reference workflow

01
Choose a Reference Image
Download both approved Omnipair reference images (below).
02
Add the Reference in Midjourney
Use Image Prompts to preserve painting style, colour, canvas texture and atmosphere.
03
Paste the ChatGPT Scene Prompt
Paste the finished single-line prompt from the Omnipair ChatGPT Prompt Formula. This defines the new scene while the reference maintains visual consistency.
04
Generate + Refine
Choose the variation that best preserves Sky / Aqua / Dawn balance, painterly texture, canvas grain and atmospheric depth. Rerun if it becomes too photorealistic, cloud-heavy or off-brand.

topics.title: Engineered glass
topics.html:
Engineered glass

Precision-built. Optically clear. Structurally believable.

Omnipair’s engineered glass makes financial ideas tangible. Defined surfaces, visible thickness and controlled reflections give each object the presence of a manufactured instrument. The material reveals the form and the relationship it represents.

01 · Start with meaning

Define the idea in one sentence before modelling: a deposit, exchange, amplification, access, verification or a unified system. Give each component a role. Show a clear destination for a deposit, a visible connection between connected parts, and a readable input/output relationship for amplification. Use symbols only when their meaning supports the message; do not imply guarantees or risk-free outcomes.

02 · Construct the surface

Build from deliberate discs, capsules, rounded rectangular solids, slots and cutouts. Keep front faces, sidewalls and bevels visibly distinct. Use consistent radii and thickness within each object family. Curves should feel controlled; avoid inflated faces, sagging contours and soft transitions that erase the construction. Symmetry can establish stability; asymmetry should describe function or movement.

03 · Preserve the mark

Retain the original symbol’s proportions, negative spaces and characteristic silhouette. Engrave, inset or extrude it with clean boundaries. Bevels and refraction must not distort it into another symbol. Choose the camera angle and focal plane so the primary mark remains recognizable at the final display size.

04 · Give glass substance

PropertyRequired treatment
ThicknessVisible depth with a clear separation between front face and sidewall.
FacesClean, stable surfaces. Broad reflections describe the planes without washing them out.
EdgesPrecisely bounded bevels that catch light and retain the silhouette.
TransparencyClear or dark-reading glass with enough contrast to reveal its volume.
RefractionInternal depth and edge complexity without scrambling the main symbol.
FinishPolished optical clarity. Local frosting only when it serves a specific purpose.

Avoid jelly, soft resin, melted plastic and bubble-like shells. Thickness alone is insufficient: the surface must feel rigid and deliberately cut.

05 · Use colour through light and depth

Anchor the treatment in Sky, Aqua and Dawn. Keep clear or neutral areas across the main face. Concentrate colour in edges, thicker sections and reflections. Blue/cyan and amber may share prominence; a fixed dominance ratio is not required. Local spectral highlights, including violet or green, are permitted as optical accents. Avoid an all-over rainbow coating or unrelated coloured fills.

06 · Light the construction

Use broad reflections to reveal faces and narrow highlights to define bevels and thickness. Preserve dark areas for contrast. Allow bright optical accents, but contain bloom so it does not dissolve edges. Glass should read through reflection, transmission and refraction; avoid a uniformly emissive neon outline. Add contact shadows where objects touch a surface.

07 · Add carbon steel where it works

Use blackened carbon steel for housings, grippers, frames, bases or connectors when the concept needs structure. Keep the finish dark and satin, with restrained machining and highlights that reveal its shape. Polished contact points are acceptable. Carbon steel does not mean carbon-fibre weave, and it is not required in every image.

08 · Match detail to the object

Simple tokens can remain minimal. Asset-specific engraving, fine relief and mechanical joints may be intricate when they preserve identity or explain function. Keep a clear hierarchy between silhouette, main symbol and secondary detail. Avoid arbitrary screws, ribs or seams added solely to suggest engineering.

09 · Compose for recognition

Choose a three-quarter view when it reveals thickness without losing the main face. Frontal and top-down views are valid when they explain the idea better. Avoid extreme perspective. Keep one dominant object or interaction, with purposeful supporting elements and generous space for copy. Floating and repeated tokens are allowed when they establish a clear relationship or hierarchy.

10 · Separate focus from softness

Selective depth of field may soften secondary objects or distant edges. Keep the main symbol and enough of the hero object’s construction in focus to read clearly. Optical blur can create depth; rounded, inflated geometry weakens the material even when rendered sharply.

11 · Keep the setting subordinate

Use near-black or dark charcoal as the default setting. Restrained Sky, Aqua and Dawn atmosphere and subtle dither or pixel texture are allowed. Keep texture outside critical edges and lettering. Avoid busy scenery, decorative particles and flares that compete with the object. Compose for the final crop and check the result at feed size.

What to avoid

12 · Keep a coherent series

Within a campaign, keep the bevel language, glass clarity, steel finish, colour behaviour, lighting direction and background treatment consistent. Match thickness within related object families rather than imposing one thickness on every form. Vary detail and camera framing to suit the message while preserving the same material character.

Before approval
  1. Silhouette: Does the form remain recognizable without its optical effects?
  2. Meaning: Can the visual’s idea be stated in one sentence?
  3. Material: Are the faces, thickness and bevels visibly solid and precise?
  4. Restraint: Does every supporting element earn its place?
  5. Recognition: Are the main icon and interaction readable at the intended size?
  6. Consistency: Does the render belong beside the approved references?

topics.title: Dither shader
topics.html:
Dither Shader

The Dither shader transforms images through a Bayer 16×16 pattern, offering precise control over size, quantization levels, brightness, and contrast. Toggle mono mode to reduce output to a single tint, defining the palette through the Mono Colour value.

The shader scales gracefully across aspect ratios and resolutions — from full-bleed hero images to compact thumbnails. Adjust the size and level parameters proportionally to maintain consistent texture density at every dimension. It is applied with the Shader feature in Figma.

Presets by output size

Common to all presets: Style Bayer 16×16 · Brightness 100% · Contrast 1 · Mono off · Mono Colour FFFFFF · 100%.
